objective: Wire the existing render-only release notes to the LIVE #poe announce channel, and give a player who replies to that announcement a path into the org. bot/release_notes.py (TASK-300-S1) already turns a commit range into one player-facing message; bot/bot.py already resolves ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL_ID for the weekly digest and already carries the whole intake path (/suggest -> scrub -> untrusted fence -> quarantine_check -> intake issue -> INTAKE_TICKET -> [DECISION] relay). Nothing about intake gets rebuilt here. Add (1) an at-most-once release announcement for a given commit range, carrying a v0 headline for the four shipped legs and a footer telling players exactly how to reach us, and (2) an on_message listener in the announce channel that answers a human reply with one short nudge toward /suggest WITHOUT ever reading message content. Also document the new configuration in bot/README.md.
constraints: bot/release_notes.py is FROZEN in this stage. Call collect_release()/render_release() exactly as they exist; compose the v0 headline and the feedback footer in bot.py, where the channel-facing code lives. If you believe render_release must change, stop and route it to pm.

This posts to a real channel watched by real people. At-most-once for a given release range is the requirement, and it beats at-least-once: reserve the range row in BOT_DB BEFORE the send and mark it posted after, so a crash mid-send never re-announces the same range.
An empty range says nothing. render_release() already returns None; when it does and the v0 headline has already gone out, record the marker and post NOTHING.
Never announce all of history. When BOT_DB has no prior range, the start of the range comes from RELEASE_SINCE_REF; if that variable is unset, log one line and no-op.

The outgoing message contains only commit subjects and issue/PR refs. Pass the composed message through the existing scrub() before sending, and put no environment values, tokens, channel ids, ledger message ids, idempotency keys, packet paths or role names in it.

The reply listener must work under discord.Intents.default(). Never read message.content, never request the privileged Message Content intent, and never file an issue from a raw reply — the nudge points the player at /suggest, which is the only intake path.
TASK-404 (issue #27, PR #30) stays PARKED under its needs-redesign [DECISION]. Do not resurrect bot/feedback.py, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL_ID, or the passive content listener.
Existing tests may be EXTENDED, never deleted or skipped. No network and no real discord connection in tests.
Branch backend/TASK-300-S2-<slug>. A literal role/... branch is refused by completion proof #4.
forbidden_actions: Requesting or documenting the privileged Message Content intent
Filing GitHub issues directly from announce-channel replies
required_checks: python3 -m pytest tests/test_announce.py tests/test_bot.py tests/test_digest.py bot/tests/test_release_notes.py -q

acceptance_criteria.text: Bot gains announce_release_once() which resolves the range (since = last recorded range end in BOT_DB, else RELEASE_SINCE_REF; until = resolved sha of RELEASE_ANNOUNCE_REF, default main), calls collect_release()/render_release(), and posts at most one message of at most 1900 characters to ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL_ID.

At-most-once is proven by test: a new release_announce table in BOT_DB keys on the range end sha, the row is reserved before the send and marked posted after, and a second call for the same range sends nothing. A test that raises mid-send proves the range is never re-announced afterwards.
Honest no-op proven by test: since == until, and a range where render_release() returns None, both send zero messages; the marker is still recorded so the range is not retried forever.
With no prior range recorded and RELEASE_SINCE_REF unset, announce_release_once() sends nothing and logs one line — never the whole history (test).

The first announcement carries a v0 headline naming the four shipped legs in player language — the engine parses a real in-game Ctrl+C item and returns a verdict, the web app gives a verdict on an item you paste yourself, the in-game overlay renders the verdict card, and Tier-2 'open details' now shows which mods actually drove the delta — and a footer telling players to use /suggest in this channel for anything wrong or missing. Subsequent announcements carry the footer but not the headline (test).

A test asserts the composed outgoing message contains no value of DISCORD_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/BOT_DB/ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL_ID, no ledger message id or idempotency key, and no tasks/packets path, and that it was passed through scrub().

on_message answers a non-bot human message in the announce channel with one short nudge toward /suggest; message.content is never read (proven by a test whose fake message raises if .content is touched); the bot's own messages and messages in any other channel produce nothing.

The nudge is rate limited to at most one per user per 6 hours from a bounded in-memory record (documented ceiling), proven by test; a restart may re-nudge at most once and that is documented, not hidden.

bot/README.md documents RELEASE_SINCE_REF, RELEASE_ANNOUNCE_REF, RELEASE_REPO_PATH (or however the git checkout path is resolved), the release_announce table, the at-most-once choice and why it beats at-least-once here, and the nudge's rate ceiling and its no-privileged-intent posture.
Both required checks pass; no test was deleted or skipped; bot/release_notes.py and bot/digest.py are byte-identical to main.
